concatenate.yes: A smith named Godo works deep in the forest. He is said to take on heavy blades and weapons other masters turn away. A young craftsman familiar with crossbows and mechanisms lives with him.
Godo keeps his forge far from the towns. He understands what a blade is for, and dislikes wasting iron on decoration. If my weapon can still be saved, he will say so plainly.
There is a house with a forge in the forest. I have not yet learned who works here.
The forge, with its hearth and workspace, is downstairs. The living quarters are above. This is the craftsmen's home, not an abandoned storehouse.
I was allowed to use a resting place. Passages must be kept clear, and the owners' tools left where they belong.
After the Eclipse, the Knight brought me here. I regained consciousness beneath this roof.
The forge has been damaged. I cannot consider my former shelter safe until I inspect what remains.
Godo worked at this forest forge. He took on heavy blades and weapons other masters refused.
Godo kept his forge far from the towns. He understood what a blade was for, and disliked wasting iron on decoration.
An enormous oak stands deep in the forest. Entangled roots conceal the earth around its trunk.
Someone searched among the roots for a stone with human features. Those who left this trail considered the find important enough to return for.
The roots divide the ground into narrow passages. Signs of someone's work end among fresh cuts. Before approaching the trunk, I should check the way back.
The stone was real. I took it from beneath the roots.
Broad galleries and narrow side tunnels branch underground. In the darkness, it is hard to judge how far the cave extends.
A scout left information about a staircase, a detour and an old support. The trail suggests they were looking here for a stone with a human face.
The ring of a stone pendant carries around corners. The creature deeper inside reacts to it. The sound may buy time if the way to the stairs is prepared beforehand.
A narrow tunnel connects to the gallery. A support obstructs the passage; its fastening can be reached from deeper within the cave.
The Behelit was found among the underground traces. I will still have to find an ordinary way out.
An abandoned camp stands among the trees, with tents and equipment belonging to people of this world.
The expedition studied an unusual find. Its records repeatedly mention dreams of a red face. A creature appeared near the tents after the sample was moved.

The wounded were moved into a separate tent. A sentry advised keeping to cover and avoiding the open ground in front of the creature. The last order was to evacuate the people and leave the equipment.
The sample was a Behelit. The expedition understood the danger too late.
A chapel stands in the forest. An old road leads to its doors.
They used to take in travelers and the wounded. Later, the inhabitants moved an unusual stone behind the altar and began calling it a miracle.
The doors were closed to those seeking help. A whisper was taken for an answer to prayer. The traces at the altar show how the wait for a miracle ended.
There is a way around the chapel. The last notes advise looking for the living instead of returning for the stone.
The stone from the reliquary was a Behelit.
The trail of missing travelers leads into a forest hollow. A creature that hunts people hides here. Before descending, I should examine the approaches and leave a way to retreat.
The creature is dead. Traces of the places it came from may remain among its remains.
The scrap I found describes a ruined foundation and a fissure in the ground. The trail leads to a separate breach.
A wound has opened in the earth among ruined foundations. Ash lies along its edges, and a heavy pulse rises from below. This is a separate passage between worlds.
The guardian fell, but the pulse has not stopped. The passage itself still needs examining.
The wound has cooled and its pulse has faded. It is quieter here. The creatures that already entered this world have not disappeared.
Among the surviving markings are routes to the Count's residence, the Black Dogs' camp and the misty valley.
The Brand remains with me.
Closing the passage has not changed what is happening to my body.
The Count's Residence
The trail led to a fortified house. The information I have calls it the Count's residence.
A fortified house behind an outer enclosure. I have not yet learned who rules it.
Behind the outward order lie executions, imprisonment and servants whose bodies can no longer be called human.
One of the prisoners described rooms he knew and a service passage. His knowledge concerns this house; he knows little of what happens beyond it.
The Count is dead. His rule over this house has ended, but the traces bound to him still need attention.
The passage at the residence is closed. This gives the surrounding area a respite, not an end to the invasion.
I accepted the Count's protection. With new flesh came a place at his court. I have yet to experience for myself what he calls protection.
Black Dogs' Camp
The trail leads to the Black Dogs' camp. The information names their commander: Wyald.
A military camp stands among the trees. I have not yet learned whom its inhabitants obey.
Here they tally spoils, hold captives and carry out the commander's orders.
Military routines survived even among monsters. People were entered alongside rations and equipment, as though all belonged on the same inventory.
Wyald is dead. His death does not undo what happened at the camp, but this master will lead no one else away.
I agreed to join the Black Dogs. Wyald promised strength and a life free of human prohibitions. My body changed at once.
The misty valley
The road leads into a misty valley. The information I received connects it with Rosine's name.
The road brought me to a misty valley. I have not yet learned who hides among its inhabitants.
Creatures called fairies circle above the flowers. The trails of missing people lead toward silk and enormous roots. This place's beauty tells me nothing certain about those who live here.
Bodies change inside the cocoons. Breaking a shell before it opens is not the same as saving whoever was once inside.
Rosine is dead. The refuge she promised will take no new victims at her bidding. One victory cannot restore those already changed.
I accepted Rosine's offer to stay among her people. The new body came at once. Human speech grew harder, and the promised safety proved no substitute for a will of my own.
Grunbeld's Fortress
The information I received connects the fortress with Grunbeld.
Heavy fortifications enclose the inner courtyard. I have not yet learned whose orders are followed here.
Grunbeld survived at the spirit tree. This trail may lead to another encounter with him.
Grunbeld died at the spirit tree. The fortress still holds the consequences of his rule and the passage bound to it.
After the battle at the spirit tree, I lost sight of him. That is not enough to consider him dead.
Grunbeld fell. The change of form prolonged his resistance, but now the battle is truly over.
The passage in the fortress is closed. The surrounding area has gained a respite.
I swore an oath to Grunbeld. He gave me a shell and a place among his warriors. With that protection came the demands of service.
House by the Spirit Tree
The trail leads to a house beside an enormous tree. The information names a witch, Flora.
A lived-in house is joined to enormous roots. Its mistress has not yet introduced herself.
Living rooms connect to enormous roots. There is space here to read, work and rest. The shelter rests on the mistress's care as well as the tree's strength.
Flora allowed me to rest and take the prepared supplies. The other things in the house belong to its inhabitants.
Flora knows about armor that lets the body keep fighting at its wearer's expense.
The house is under attack. Its former defenses no longer hold back every enemy. The familiar passages are now ways out.
I escaped the house. Fire and battle remained behind me. What survived is still unknown.
The house by the spirit tree is lost. Fire passed through familiar rooms. This place can no longer be the refuge it was.
Living rooms were connected to enormous roots. There was space here to read, work and rest. The shelter rested on the mistress's care as well as the tree's strength.
Flora spoke of armor that lets the body keep fighting at its wearer's expense.
I chose a place to return to from the road. Water, dressings and a clear way out should always remain here.
A sign of stones and bones stands near my sleeping place. It restrains the Brand's nighttime call nearby, but does not stop creatures already here.
My former shelter is no longer fit for rest. I will need to find another.
Godo owns the forest forge. He speaks sharply and gets down to business quickly. First he wants to see the weapon, then hear requests about it.
Godo recognized me. He still grumbles about my blades and doesn't mince words. He judges iron more confidently than others judge people.
His work is blades, iron fittings and repairs. He leaves mechanisms and crossbows to Rickert.
He took me in when I could not cross the threshold on my own. He asked no payment for water or a place by the wall.
At the forge, Godo spoke of fire and sparks. A bright flash soon dies; work and those you care for remain. What matters is not only the strength of a blow, but the life you intend to return to.
I chose not to listen to his talk by the forge.
Godo refused to make this blade for me. He knows of the power I accepted, and believes I must now answer for my choice.
Godo owned the forest forge. He spoke sharply and got down to business quickly. First he wanted to see the weapon, then hear requests about it.
Godo recognized me. He grumbled about my blades and didn't mince words. He judged iron more confidently than others judged people.
His work was blades, iron fittings and repairs. He left mechanisms and crossbows to Rickert.
Godo refused to make this blade for me. He knew of the power I accepted, and believed I must now answer for my choice.
Godo is dead.
Rickert works alongside Godo. He understands crossbows, triggers and fastenings. He can spend a long time on a small part if a weapon's reliability depends on it.
He traveled with the Band of the Hawk. In battle, he relies on a crossbow, position and preparation more than on the force of a sword stroke.
Rickert helped me after my rescue. He did not know what had happened inside the Eclipse.
I told him what I saw in the Eclipse. He learned of Griffith's betrayal and the deaths of his comrades.
I told Rickert the band died in an attack by men and beasts. I kept Griffith's betrayal from him.
I have not yet told him what I endured. He is left with questions about his comrades' fate.
I admitted that I had lied. Rickert now knows the truth and remembers my deception. One admission is not enough to make everything as it was.
Trust has become possible between us again. That has not erased our earlier conversation from memory.
Rickert decided to travel with me. He agreed to be a companion, not someone's property.
After what I said, Rickert refused to travel with me. Ordinary work at the forge remained a separate matter.
Rickert worked alongside Godo. He understood crossbows, triggers and fastenings. He could spend a long time on a small part if a weapon's reliability depended on it.
He traveled with the Band of the Hawk. In battle, he relied on a crossbow, position and preparation more than on the force of a sword stroke.
Rickert is dead.
A rider whose helmet resembles a skull. He found a passage out of the place of sacrifice and carried me through.
He said he had an opportunity to intervene and took it. He demanded no new debt for the life he saved.
He has long fought beings from beyond. He gave neither his name nor his history.
The Knight continued on his way. He warned me not to expect him to wait at this threshold again.

concatenate: Words recorded after speaking with the Skull Knight.
The Knight carried me out of the sacrifice. Escape did not undo its consequences.
Godot works on blades; Rickert works on crossbows and mechanisms at the woodland forge.
You saw the boundary where greatness is bought with other lives. Those who rose above the crowd accepted that harvest. Those feasting beneath the throne merely did what they had been permitted.

Many were. They rejected their nature when an earthly existence was no longer enough. Their old failings and desires remained. Sometimes those human habits make the monsters recognizable. And vulnerable.
Their altered flesh can be destroyed. Do not mistake their bodies for true immortality. Nor should you look for human mercy where the abyss rules.
Wait before you step forward. Study how the enemy moves, what it protects and when it must pause for breath. Know where you will retreat. Blind fury is no substitute for a way back.
The God Hand. Do not confuse them with the servants admitted to the feast. Killing an ordinary apostle does not bring their overthrow a step closer.
If I thought your struggle useless, I would not have carried you out of that hell.
This land had already been wounded by its own end of the world. Another darkness seeps through the open wounds. The boundary has thinned, making your home accessible to hungrier predators.
The past cannot be restored, even if every passage is sealed. But you can keep the next traveler from meeting the same fate.
He took the throne offered to him. Your memories of the man cannot explain the abyss into which he was reborn.
Then first learn to live until the next dawn. Otherwise your oath of vengeance will be no more than the last words of a man dying in the night.
Do not expect what you witnessed to be the last expression of that will. Your concern now is to endure the threat already following you.
You dispersed a reflection. It could take his shape and carry some of his power, but it was not the being you seek.
The shape that stood before you will threaten no one else. That matters. But do not credit your victory with something it did not accomplish.
A face is not enough. Consider where it came from, what holds it here and what it leaves behind. A vanished shadow is not proof of an original death.
While the boundaries between worlds remain broken, I would not call that encounter the last.
The Brand remains a mark of sacrifice. Beings beyond the boundary can discern it where a human eye sees nothing. Night makes their journey to you easier.

Pain and blood may come before a creature appears, especially a powerful one. Heed that warning, but do not expect it to name your enemy or show a safe road. The Brand is no friend to you. It simply is.
Not every night is the same. Sometimes you will hear only footsteps beyond a wall. Sometimes you will have to abandon your shelter and run. Silence does not mean they have forgotten you.
Find a place you can leave. Do not corner yourself for the imagined safety of walls. Prepare light, dressings and weapons. Keep what you need close: there will be no time to pack when you must flee.
Against some of them, yes. But an ordinary wall cannot keep out everything that comes from the darkness. Some creatures need no door.
Dawn may end the pursuit itself. It does not promise to destroy those that already reached you. Look at what remains outside before opening the door.
A bone and stone sign hinders the Brand's night summons nearby. It does not remove creatures already here and does not replace shelter.
More peacefully. Not carelessly. Even a protected place must have an exit. Never make the sign your last hope.
Arrange eight stones and four bones into a sign on clear ground. Keep it close to your sleeping place. Its protection stays on the same level; it will not drive away creatures already here.
No. You will close one road into this world, and that matters to those who live nearby. The mark on your body belongs to another bond. Closing a breach does not break it.
Recover before a fight. Prepare for night, then follow a trail you know. Do not take on every enemy at once.
Judeau saw other people even when everything around him was turning them into prey.
Sometimes a man knows he cannot hold the enemy. Still he stands between it and those who can escape.
A victim has a life that cannot fit inside the word victim. Desires, failings, arguments. Do not give the monsters that part of him as well.
Such hopes are easily lost behind banners and the names of commanders. To him that future mattered no less than another man's dream of a kingdom.
Not enough to stop all that happened. But you do not know how much time his act gave someone else.
Then preserve more than how he died. Preserve who he was.
I call it an act that cannot be measured only by who remained standing.
You may carry that thought all your life. It cannot put you beside him that night. Decide whom you will stand beside now.
Grief does not require that you agreed on everything in life.
They did not need to become heroes to deserve their lives.
Yes. You see not only a death but everything that can never follow it.
Keep it, give it to someone who knew him, or leave it in a worthy place. Memory does not demand you always carry its weight.
One who has long walked against them.
No. But for now it tells you more than a name.
I had the chance to intervene. I took it.
I did not carry you out of one bargain to immediately bind you to another.
Knowing of a disaster and having the power to stop it are not the same.
I am not asking you to accept it. But do not base your next step on the belief that someone could have fixed everything with a single blow.
Enough humanity remains in me to remember what I fight against.
Not every story needs to be told at another man's threshold.
You are alive and asking that question. Begin there.
No. But your choice still belongs to you. Do not give it away merely because you cannot rule everything else.
I have my own road. Our enemies will not wait for you to recover.
Perhaps. But do not build your life around waiting for me.

'The Behelit opened a place of sacrifice along the boundary where our worlds collided. Your Eclipse widened those wounds; it did not create this world's first catastrophe. I could not undo the sacrifice. I cut a way out while someone remained to save.'

The Behelit was a key to a place of sacrifice. The lives offered there were not a toll that bought your safety. You escaped because a way out was cut while you still lived. Do not seek another ceremony as a cure for what it left you.

'The Brand marks a survivor of the sacrifice. Its pain warns you when demons draw near; a stronger presence hurts more. At night, expect them to seek you out. Find cover and leave yourself a way to flee.'

Not every demon follows your Brand. Some have crossed the wounds between worlds and roam on their own; the Brand draws another hunt toward you at night. Quieting its call does not remove creatures already near your bed. A closed wound does not silence the Brand.

A sign of stone and bone quiets the Brand’s new night summons within eight tiles on the same level. It does not stop roaming demons, zombies or attacks. Place your bed within its reach; prepare water, light and an escape route. The sign needs no fuel, but its protection ends when you leave its reach.

Set eight stones and four bones into a protective sign on clear ground. A little wilderness knowledge is enough to arrange it; allow about twenty minutes. Keep your bed within eight steps on the same level. Walls and a clear escape route must do what the sign cannot: shelter you from creatures already here.

Choose a place you can leave as well as defend. Dress your wounds, keep drinking water and bandages near your bed, and leave room to reach the door. Light helps you see what is coming; it is not a ward. Rest before testing your strength against an apostle. A weapon cannot give you back the breath spent running.

Walk the outer ground first. Look for cover, lesser creatures and a way back before entering the keeper’s ground. Watch a heavy attack begin; move aside rather than trade blows through it. A retreat is not a broken oath. Return when your wounds and your equipment allow it, then examine what the fight uncovered.

A keeper holds a particular wound open. When it falls, examine that wound; a victory alone may leave the opening behind. Closing it restrains new crossings nearby. Creatures that have already crossed remain, and distant wounds still feed the dark. Take the evidence with you and read it before choosing another road.

The collision broke more than the ground. Some lives were drawn away from the deaths that awaited them. That does not make every being here a projection. Kill a living original and that life ends; breaking a reflection leaves its source untouched.

'Apostles are monstrous beings with wills and bodies of their own. The God Hand stand apart: they preside over the sacrifice. Void and Griffith are not ordinary apostles. Do not mistake surviving an encounter for defeating them.'
'Some things you met before were projections: an echo formed around a Behelit. Breaking the echo leaves the true being untouched. The Behelit itself was real.'

Read a recovered letter before setting it aside; a sealed page has told you nothing. If a road is uncertain, keep its entry and return to the evidence. When we part, those notes will remain with you.

I follow a war older than your wounds. When I can deny the sacrifice another life, I do. That does not make your road mine to command. Keep the life I carried out of the dark; decide what is worth protecting with it.

concatenate.yes: Flora is a witch who lives by the spirit tree. She speaks calmly and does not promise deliverance from every misfortune. For her, knowledge is bound to care for the living.
She explained that the Brand connects its bearer to another side of the world. Simply defeating one monster does not sever that bond.
Flora knows the price of the Berserker Armor. It can force the body to keep fighting when an ordinary person could no longer stand.
She allowed me to take the prepared aid. It is a gift from the mistress of the house, not permission to empty it.
Flora learned of my change. She did not promise to restore my former body. Discussing how to use the will I still have proved more important than a promise of easy healing.
Flora was a witch who lived by the spirit tree. She spoke calmly and did not promise deliverance from every misfortune. For her, knowledge was bound to care for the living.
Flora knew the price of the Berserker Armor. It can force the body to keep fighting when an ordinary person could no longer stand.
Flora is dead.
A man held in the Count's residence. He knows the servants' habits and some of the service rooms. He fears the master and doubts that outside help is even possible.
He told me what he could about a way through the house. His help made it clearer where the servants could be bypassed.
The Count's hold over him is ended. What he will do with that freedom is not yet known.
A man held in the Count's residence. He knew the servants' habits and some of the service rooms. He feared the master and doubted that outside help was even possible.
The prisoner is dead.
Work here is paid for with usable metal and other needed materials. Godo handles blades; Rickert handles mechanisms and bolts. It is worth discussing an agreement before bringing random scrap.
Materials go to the craftsman who accepted the job. Finished work takes time. When it is done, I must return to the forge to collect it.
Godo will not reforge a sound blade without need. First he examines the edge and says whether work is required. If the damage is serious, it will take materials and time at the forge.
I must leave the blade itself for repair. While the smith has it, I will need another weapon on the road. Once the work is finished, I will get my blade back.
A long fighting blade without ornament. Such a sword needs reliable tempering and good balance. Size alone does not make good work.
My homemade blade follows the general design, but it is heavier, rougher and less durable in use. This is my attempt, not Godo's work.
Godo made a blade for an impossible task: killing a dragon. An ordinary warrior can barely lift this iron. The smith does not speak of it as a handsome parade weapon.
Rickert can assemble a mechanical replacement for a lost hand. The device combines a moving mechanism with a concealed cannon. The work requires precise fastenings as well as iron.
The device is finished, but has not yet become part of my arm. Before relying on it in battle, I must fit it and check the mechanism.
The prosthesis is fitted to my arm. I must get used to its weight and movement, and keep the cannon working and loaded with suitable charges.
I assembled this mechanism myself.
I assembled it after losing my hand. Rickert remarked on that work in particular.
Rickert explained how to assemble a mechanical replacement for a lost hand. The device combines a moving mechanism with a concealed cannon. The work requires precise fastenings as well as iron.
Rickert values a reliable trigger more than a showy modification. A crossbow helps keep distance, but requires a suitable position and time to reload.
I can commission bolts from him by supplying the materials. Discussing bolts does not oblige me to order a prosthesis or invite Rickert on the road.
A small stone with human features. It is hard to mistake it for an ordinary trinket.
The accounts of those who held it before repeatedly mention whispers and the feeling of a foreign call.
Now I too have heard the call. It speaks to a desire that is difficult to say aloud.
Blood changed the stone. The call grew more insistent. It promises a different way out of the ceremony, but no return to my former life.
I was warned: the passage is dangerous even to one who refuses the offered power. Changes may remain forever.
I passed through a place of sacrifice. The band I knew before that night was among the doomed. Griffith stood on the other side of what happened.
Beyond the passage lay a place of sacrifice. People and traces of a last resistance lay among the creatures. Their past was not mine, but what I saw has become part of my life.
The Skull Knight carried me out. The ceremony stayed behind; its consequences stayed with me.
That night, I lost my left hand.
That night, I lost an eye.
I managed to destroy the form holding the scene together. That was not the destruction of the entire God Hand.
Five figures waited at the end of the path. They spoke of fate, desires and choice. The offered gift did not promise to preserve my former body.
I could accept the gift, but could not decree the form it would give me.
I agreed. The participants in the ceremony returned me outside. Now the change continues within me.
I refused even after the final warning. They returned me without the gift. The human body did not endure that passage without consequences.

concatenate.yes: Void spoke of causality and a decision that cannot be undone. The stone brought me to a choice, but did not make its consequences someone else's responsibility.
Slan spoke of the desire to live and a body able to receive more than a human could. In her promises, flesh and passion sounded like a single price.
Ubik turned to memory and to how easily a person explains their own desire to themselves. His words made me doubt not only what I saw, but my own excuses.
Conrad spoke little. In his answers, human vulnerability seemed part of inevitable decay. He promised no departure from this place without consequences.
Femto spoke as though the former human measure no longer mattered. The strength he offered did not make its recipient equal to the one offering it.
I returned human. Refusal left me no accepted power, but the ceremony still changed how I hear, see or experience my surroundings.
Some sounds have grown muffled. I have to listen closely to hear familiar things.
My sight is no longer what it was before the passage.
A tremor that was not there before has entered precise movements.
Memories return uninvited. Sometimes the present briefly loses its hold before them.
The sense of danger remains even where I cannot yet see anything.
The Brand remains the mark of a sacrifice. Beings beyond the boundary see it where human eyes see nothing. Night eases their way to the marked.
Pain and blood may warn of a nearby creature. The warning does not name the enemy or reveal a safe road.
Closing one passage does not sever the Brand's bond.
Silence does not mean the trail is lost. I should prepare a resting place before dark and keep essential things near the exit.
A door will not stop every creature. The protection of walls must not leave me without a way to retreat.
Dawn does not destroy creatures that already arrived. Before stepping outside, I must look for those still there.
A small sign of stones and bones restrains the Brand's nighttime call nearby. It does not destroy creatures or replace walls, water and a way out.
The sign requires eight stones and four bones. It is built on clear ground near a sleeping place.
The bed should remain near the sign and on the same floor. The sign works under open sky too, but that does not make an open clearing a reliable shelter.
The boundary between worlds is damaged. Creatures that did not belong to these lands before arrive through separate passages.
Defeating the creature holding a passage does not always close the wound itself. After the battle, I must examine what it left.
A closed passage gives the surrounding area a respite. Creatures already here remain, and distant wounds still exist.
Not every familiar shape belongs to the being itself. Reflections bearing part of another's power arise at the boundaries between worlds.
The reflection of Griffith I defeated was not the original. The disappearance of its shape does not prove the death of the one whose image it took.
The stone I found was real, though the creature around it was a reflection.
Among the traces of the last battle, I recognized Judeau. Even there, he tried to buy others time. He deserves to be remembered for more than that last night.
I found evidence of Judeau. The traces suggest he tried to help others escape the crush. Before that night he had a life I know only in fragments.
The hilt of his knife survived.
The Knight said that keeping a person's memory means remembering how they lived, not only how they died.
Pippin held the passage to the end. Others could still get away behind the place where he stood.
The traces by Pippin's body show resistance in a narrow passage. He stayed between the creatures and those still trying to escape.
A broken clasp survived among the fragments.
Not every deed can be measured by who remains standing after the battle.
Corkus wanted to escape war and mud. We often disagreed, but that does not diminish what was taken from him.
The evidence of Corkus holds ordinary human hopes. Monsters cut them short just as they did the dreams of those called heroes.
A piece of his scabbard survived.
No one has to become a hero to deserve a life.
Gaston wanted to leave war behind one day and live by his own work. His future was quieter than others' dreams of a kingdom, but meant no less to him.
I found the trace of a man named Gaston. He hoped for an ordinary life after the war. Such hopes are easily lost amid great names and banners.
His sewing tools recall the life he wanted to return to.
This armor lets the wearer fight beyond ordinary pain. It does not leave the body unharmed or cancel the price of wounds already received.
Obtaining the armor does not mean learning to resist it. The power holding a body in battle can destroy its wearer.
I already have the complete armor. I need understanding and control, not a second set.
I have part of the armor. It is not yet a complete set.
Flora refused to give me new armor after my choice. She knows of the power I accepted.
I escaped, but the house by the spirit tree is lost. Beyond its familiar doors lie rooms where, only recently, one could rest and talk.
Closed wounds brought a local respite. They did not stop the worlds colliding. The road continues among consequences that can still be changed.
The trail leads to Grunbeld's fortress.
Grunbeld is dead. The fortress still holds the passage bound to him and the consequences of his rule.
I do not know what became of Grunbeld after the battle.
The wounds whose trails I followed are closed. Those places have grown quieter. This is not the end of darkness, but people have gained time they did not have before.

The known roads of this journey are traveled. Not every decision was a victory: an accepted pact left its trace too. Where breaches closed, the surrounding areas gained a respite. Other wounds and creatures already here have not disappeared.
The Brand remains. The next night still requires preparation.
The power I accepted remains with me. A finished hunt does not restore a former body.
I remained human and carry the consequences of that passage.
I have already agreed. I feel the change, but do not yet know its final shape. No one offered to let me return for another share of power.
The change continues on its own. New sensations and needs do not appear at once. The body's greater endurance does not mean it has stopped being wounded.
I took the flesh of a defeated creature into myself. It did not remain ordinary food. Now its strength is changing my body.
This choice leads no way back. Accepting different flesh in place of the first does not undo what has already happened.
Bone emerged beneath the scar, tendons stretched and fingers straightened. My left hand grew back. This came with the accepted change, not ordinary healing.
The cannon mechanism stayed on my forearm. The new hand did not destroy the device already fitted there.
My body lengthened and my fingers changed. Distance sometimes feels unlike what the eye sees. A short step can carry me through a gap I once would have crossed another way.
A bend in space can soften a blow, but the flesh itself is not invulnerable. Ordinary rigid gloves no longer fit my hands.
My flesh has grown stronger and more supple. I can draw from it a weapon I did not have before. Regaining strength costs hunger and time.
Rigid equipment on my hands obstructs the changed body. The ability to recover is no reason to forget wounds and food.
My silhouette has become harder to hold in view. I can turn another's attention toward a false target and briefly disrupt an enemy's perception.
This promises no mastery over every mind. Ordinary rigid helmets and masks do not fit my changed head.
My flesh has grown thicker and heavier. My touch corrodes living bodies, and my breath leaves a caustic haze. My own strength demands care near those I do not want to hurt.
I move more slowly. Ordinary rigid armor for the torso and legs does not fit my new body. A cloud is not safe merely because I released it.
Dark wings changed my back and balance. My movement is swifter. With pressure, I can push an opponent back and disrupt their advance.
The wings need room. Ordinary torso clothing obstructs them; this strength has not given me endless flight.
My body has grown heavy and pliable. The changed flesh endures more, and its tendril can reach an enemy within striking distance.
Durability costs slowness. Rigid armor constricts my torso and arms. Recovery remains a bodily need, not proof of immortality.
The new body strains toward a lunge and a grasp. Close combat has become more natural; precise work, harder.
After exertion, strength returns more slowly. My changed hands and feet do not fit ordinary rigid gloves and footwear.
Insectlike wings unfolded behind my back. They help me move quickly and soften a fall, if my body and burden allow their use.
I have not gained free ascent into the sky. Heavy and tight equipment obstructs my wings, and my body's fragility has not vanished.
A heavy carapace closed over my body. Heat has become easier to endure, and my breath can become flame.
My body needs more food and recovers from exertion more slowly. Rigid armor will not fit over the shell. Resistance to heat does not make every fire safe.
The Count called me his. My body grew denser and slower, and a tendril grew from it. The new protection is bound to the one who gave it.
My changed torso will not fit ordinary rigid armor. I accepted a place at another's court, but must still answer for my own actions.
Wyald gave me a beast's body. It strains forward toward a short rush and a blow. Crude strength costs clumsiness at precise work.
Rigid gloves do not fit my changed hands. His approval is no substitute for rest after battle.
Rosine accepted me among her people. My head and hands changed; words grew harder. I can still choose and act.
My former human work takes more effort. Ordinary rigid helmets, masks and gloves do not fit this body.
The oath I accepted left a shell on my body. It withstands some blows and heat, but makes movement heavier.
Ordinary rigid armor constricts my torso and arms. Beneath the master's protection remain the demands of service.
My bond with the master no longer gives its former support. The changed body remains. A broken oath did not make me human again.
The master is dead. With him, the support ended, but the flesh I accepted from him has not vanished.
The rebuilding is finished. My body has taken its new shape. Now I must live with it, not wait for another night to restore my former self.
The Count is dead. He will give no more orders or offer a helping hand. There is no one left to offer one.
The body you received from him has not gone away. It is yours now, truly yours, with no master behind your back.
Wyald is dead. His voice will no longer summon the pack. It is probably already prowling on its own, without a leader.
What he gave you remains yours. The death of the one who changed you does not undo the change.
Rosine is gone. You must now make sense of the home she promised with your own mind, without her voice behind your shoulder.
Your human body has not returned. And it will not.
Grunbeld is dead. There will be no new orders. No one is left to give them.
The shell he gave remains part of your flesh, just as before.
A heavy seal left by the Count. Worn, it helps strike beings from beyond the boundary. Its power is not directed against every living body.
A sinewy knot sharpens the sense of what moves in darkness. With it, the night road is easier to make out.
A thin veil retains a trace of the strange valley. Worn, it helps evade a blow, but promises no escape from every attack.
The shard belongs to the apostle itself. Worn, it helps endure heat, but does not protect against smoke or make fire safe.
It cannot be confused with the charred clasps of the garrison's people.
The wheel broke before dusk. The iron fastenings were left beneath the iron-bound chest; the grain was taken.
An order is tucked between the pages: "Take the bent blades to Godo's forest forge. A young crossbow maker works with him. Follow the old cart tracks through the woods."
Turns and crossings are marked in the margins.

Something watches the open clearing. I saw trees move without wind. I tied my pack above the washout and took the lower path to check the other bank. If I don't return, keep to the rocks and leave enough room to turn back.
We're leaving before the next dusk. The water is clean; those who follow may need the blanket more than we do.

The smith Godo repaired our broken blade. His young helper makes crossbow bolts. We wrote down the return route here: the old path, the stream crossing, then the charcoal burners' trail. It's a long walk, but there's a craftsman at the end of the road.
Clean cloth for dressings must be boiled. A waterskin is best sewn before a long journey. Drinking water, a sleeping place and a clear exit matter more than a comfortable room.
A small sign of stone and bone helps restrain the nighttime call, but does not drive away a creature already standing at the door.
Flora compares the joined worlds to roots grown together across a wound. A quiet place can shelter a traveler; one refuge cannot heal the whole world.
Traces of smoke remain in the margins. Most of the research lay beyond the torn pages.
A wooden bookmark shaped like a leaf survived in a stone niche among the roots. Carved into it are the words: "Leave a light for the next traveler."
Between the charred edges are a broken road, a ruined foundation and markings around a fissure. The creature from the hollow carried this route to another breach.
Fresh cuts end midway through the roots. Two rows of notches are carved into the handle; one stops abruptly. These people tried to cut a path to the stone face, not fight what lived beneath it.
The inscription names two travelers and asks that both return home. The second knot was tied by a trembling hand. On the bark nearby is a dark stain like the one on the discarded root cutter.
We left the cart on the old path. The face is caught in the roots, just as he said. While the creature circled the trunk, I waited behind the thick roots and didn't move.
We'll return by the old western path. If only one of us reaches the cart, leave the other's name on the cord.
Dry the herbs separately. Boil clean cloth for wounds. Mend old sleeves before the next journey. Keep both passages around the spirit tree clear.
A refuge remains a refuge because someone cares for it.

I marked the broad gallery to the east. Beneath it, a narrow tunnel skirts the rock and joins the gallery twice. In the western hall we heard the pendant before we saw what followed its sound. The bends hid us from its eyes.
There is a passage with a support near the stairs, but the peg faces deeper into the cave. If we make it, I'll leave another mark by the broken prop.

Water was stored in the eastern room, blankets and dressings in the vestry. An early entry mentions a traveler with a repaired sword and bolts: "Godo's forge is still working in the forest. The old man and his young helper take usable metal in payment." He drew the road on the back.
Later, instead of food portions, they began counting hours beside the red stone. The last volunteer wrote: "This was meant to be a refuge."
We called the stone a miracle because we needed a miracle. We moved it behind the altar and stopped opening the door to strangers. When the whispering began, we decided we had been answered.
The handprints on the altar were not left during prayer.

If the chapel is lost, leave through the breach in the western wall. An old rut farther into the forest leads to a great oak with tangled roots. Travelers spoke of another stone face. I have not seen it myself.
The extraction order is crossed out.

Three of us described the same red face after spending the night here. When we moved the sample, scratching began behind the new tent. Pavel is wounded: the creature caught him when he stepped into the open. Cancel sample collection. Send transport for the wounded. We are leaving the equipment.

A note in the margin reads: "If we get out, find the smith Godo. He and his young helper repaired our fittings and crossbow. The route to his forest forge is marked on the back." A list of turns and a stream crossing follows.
We broke shields to build a wall. Held the passage until the wounded were carried through. There is no road back. Don't lose sight of the pale path. Enormous ribs lean toward the gathering place.

The names recur on execution notices. Shoes and cloaks were sorted before sentencing, as though their owner had already ceased to be a person. One entry was crossed out and replaced with "sent below."
Behind every neat column was a person they had already decided was a thing.
The first pages concern boiled linen and ordinary wounds. Then sketches appear of a second mouth growing from a servant's chest.
The author stopped calling it a disease. Pieces of the master's flesh implanted another life in the victim. Familiar treatments did not restore the person.
The ribbon lay beside sewing and a book kept free of dust. A note calls the room Theresia's and forbids the servants to disturb it.
The same ruler who signed the prison lists protected this little island of ordinary life. It does not say where his daughter is now.
Two roads are marked on the map. One bears the Black Dogs' camp and Wyald's name; the other, a misty valley and Rosine's. Notes about missing caravans and closed roads run along the edge.
The lists separate soldiers, prisoners and those taken to the commander. The first pages record boot sizes and rations. Later notes describe distorted guards wearing the same uniforms.
Another life of the camp shows through the familiar military ledger.
I hid this before roll call. The cage doors are tied, not locked with iron keys. Untie them from either side and pass through. The route through the quarry is longer, but open.
At the bottom, a short word has been added beside one name: "escaped."

Wyald ordered the plundered supplies counted and a space cleared for fighting. Wooden barriers were dragged to the edges. Between the lines about spoils and people, one demand recurs: no one leaves without his permission.
The last sheet speaks of a fractured world. The crossing changed the commander's former fate. The one living in this camp is the man himself, not his reflection.
They called the winged things fairies because the flowers were beautiful. I followed a trail of abandoned shoes, past the games, toward the silk.
In the quiet shells, no hope remained. In the moving ones was something already changed. I cannot bring them back. The western ravine offers a way around the grove to the enormous roots.
The ribbon was tied to a branch as a marker for a game. Farther on, the same knot is caught in a split shell. The flowers kept growing after the games stopped.
Sometimes all a person leaves is a thing easily walked past.

Mikhail, if you reach the camp first: we moved the wounded to the southwest tent. The creature came out of the northern tent and caught Pavel in the open. Keep behind the tent walls and leave through the gap in the eastern fence. We are leaving before dusk.
Lena.
The last prayer is crossed out.

We barred the main doors to keep strangers out. Now footsteps sound inside. Irina carried the remaining blankets through the vestry; I couldn't persuade her to return for the stone. The western wall is breached. Follow the living while there is still time.

The eastern passage is wide enough to carry him, but the scratches there are fresh. I left the iron crowbar by the broken support. We circled the stone pendant and approached the prop from below. The peg can be pulled out from that side.
If he wakes, first we'll try to reach the stairs, not the red face.
A charred clasp is all that remains of the garrison banner. Names of the people who held the southern road are scratched on the back.
This is a human possession. The apostle's fiery shell did not belong to those whose names remain here.

Clean cloth for dressings must be boiled. A waterskin is best sewn before a long journey. Drinking water, a sleeping place and a clear exit matter more than a comfortable room.
A small sign of stone and bone helps restrain the nighttime call, but does not drive away a creature already standing at the door.

A heavy seal left by the Count. Worn, it helps strike beings from beyond the boundary. Its power is not directed against every living body.
The wounds whose trails I followed are closed. Those places have grown quieter. This is not the end of darkness, but people have gained time they did not have before.

The known roads of this journey are traveled. Not every decision was a victory: an accepted pact left its trace too. Where breaches closed, the surrounding areas gained a respite. Other wounds and creatures already here have not disappeared.
The Brand remains. The next night still requires preparation.
The power I accepted remains with me. A finished hunt does not restore a former body.
I remained human and carry the consequences of that passage.
A rider whose helmet resembles a skull. He found a passage out of the place of sacrifice and carried me through.
He said he had an opportunity to intervene and took it. He demanded no new debt for the life he saved.
He has long fought beings from beyond. He gave neither his name nor his history.
The Knight continued on his way. He warned me not to expect him to wait at this threshold again.

concatenate: Words recorded after speaking with the Skull Knight.
The Knight carried me out of the sacrifice. Escape did not undo its consequences.
Godot works on blades; Rickert works on crossbows and mechanisms at the woodland forge.
You saw the boundary where greatness is bought with other lives. Those who rose above the crowd accepted that harvest. Those feasting beneath the throne merely did what they had been permitted.

Many were. They rejected their nature when an earthly existence was no longer enough. Their old failings and desires remained. Sometimes those human habits make the monsters recognizable. And vulnerable.
Their altered flesh can be destroyed. Do not mistake their bodies for true immortality. Nor should you look for human mercy where the abyss rules.
Wait before you step forward. Study how the enemy moves, what it protects and when it must pause for breath. Know where you will retreat. Blind fury is no substitute for a way back.
The God Hand. Do not confuse them with the servants admitted to the feast. Killing an ordinary apostle does not bring their overthrow a step closer.
If I thought your struggle useless, I would not have carried you out of that hell.
This land had already been wounded by its own end of the world. Another darkness seeps through the open wounds. The boundary has thinned, making your home accessible to hungrier predators.
The past cannot be restored, even if every passage is sealed. But you can keep the next traveler from meeting the same fate.
He took the throne offered to him. Your memories of the man cannot explain the abyss into which he was reborn.
Then first learn to live until the next dawn. Otherwise your oath of vengeance will be no more than the last words of a man dying in the night.
Do not expect what you witnessed to be the last expression of that will. Your concern now is to endure the threat already following you.
You dispersed a reflection. It could take his shape and carry some of his power, but it was not the being you seek.
The shape that stood before you will threaten no one else. That matters. But do not credit your victory with something it did not accomplish.
A face is not enough. Consider where it came from, what holds it here and what it leaves behind. A vanished shadow is not proof of an original death.
While the boundaries between worlds remain broken, I would not call that encounter the last.
The Brand remains a mark of sacrifice. Beings beyond the boundary can discern it where a human eye sees nothing. Night makes their journey to you easier.

Pain and blood may come before a creature appears, especially a powerful one. Heed that warning, but do not expect it to name your enemy or show a safe road. The Brand is no friend to you. It simply is.
Not every night is the same. Sometimes you will hear only footsteps beyond a wall. Sometimes you will have to abandon your shelter and run. Silence does not mean they have forgotten you.
Find a place you can leave. Do not corner yourself for the imagined safety of walls. Prepare light, dressings and weapons. Keep what you need close: there will be no time to pack when you must flee.
Against some of them, yes. But an ordinary wall cannot keep out everything that comes from the darkness. Some creatures need no door.
Dawn may end the pursuit itself. It does not promise to destroy those that already reached you. Look at what remains outside before opening the door.
A bone and stone sign hinders the Brand's night summons nearby. It does not remove creatures already here and does not replace shelter.
More peacefully. Not carelessly. Even a protected place must have an exit. Never make the sign your last hope.
Arrange eight stones and four bones into a sign on clear ground. Keep it close to your sleeping place. Its protection stays on the same level; it will not drive away creatures already here.
No. You will close one road into this world, and that matters to those who live nearby. The mark on your body belongs to another bond. Closing a breach does not break it.
Recover before a fight. Prepare for night, then follow a trail you know. Do not take on every enemy at once.
Judeau saw other people even when everything around him was turning them into prey.
Sometimes a man knows he cannot hold the enemy. Still he stands between it and those who can escape.
A victim has a life that cannot fit inside the word victim. Desires, failings, arguments. Do not give the monsters that part of him as well.
Such hopes are easily lost behind banners and the names of commanders. To him that future mattered no less than another man's dream of a kingdom.
Not enough to stop all that happened. But you do not know how much time his act gave someone else.
Then preserve more than how he died. Preserve who he was.
I call it an act that cannot be measured only by who remained standing.
You may carry that thought all your life. It cannot put you beside him that night. Decide whom you will stand beside now.
Grief does not require that you agreed on everything in life.
They did not need to become heroes to deserve their lives.
Yes. You see not only a death but everything that can never follow it.
Keep it, give it to someone who knew him, or leave it in a worthy place. Memory does not demand you always carry its weight.
One who has long walked against them.
No. But for now it tells you more than a name.
I had the chance to intervene. I took it.
I did not carry you out of one bargain to immediately bind you to another.
Knowing of a disaster and having the power to stop it are not the same.
I am not asking you to accept it. But do not base your next step on the belief that someone could have fixed everything with a single blow.
Enough humanity remains in me to remember what I fight against.
Not every story needs to be told at another man's threshold.
You are alive and asking that question. Begin there.
No. But your choice still belongs to you. Do not give it away merely because you cannot rule everything else.
I have my own road. Our enemies will not wait for you to recover.
Perhaps. But do not build your life around waiting for me.

'The Behelit opened a place of sacrifice along the boundary where our worlds collided. Your Eclipse widened those wounds; it did not create this world's first catastrophe. I could not undo the sacrifice. I cut a way out while someone remained to save.'

The Behelit was a key to a place of sacrifice. The lives offered there were not a toll that bought your safety. You escaped because a way out was cut while you still lived. Do not seek another ceremony as a cure for what it left you.

'The Brand marks a survivor of the sacrifice. Its pain warns you when demons draw near; a stronger presence hurts more. At night, expect them to seek you out. Find cover and leave yourself a way to flee.'

Not every demon follows your Brand. Some have crossed the wounds between worlds and roam on their own; the Brand draws another hunt toward you at night. Quieting its call does not remove creatures already near your bed. A closed wound does not silence the Brand.

A sign of stone and bone quiets the Brand’s new night summons within eight tiles on the same level. It does not stop roaming demons, zombies or attacks. Place your bed within its reach; prepare water, light and an escape route. The sign needs no fuel, but its protection ends when you leave its reach.

Set eight stones and four bones into a protective sign on clear ground. A little wilderness knowledge is enough to arrange it; allow about twenty minutes. Keep your bed within eight steps on the same level. Walls and a clear escape route must do what the sign cannot: shelter you from creatures already here.

Choose a place you can leave as well as defend. Dress your wounds, keep drinking water and bandages near your bed, and leave room to reach the door. Light helps you see what is coming; it is not a ward. Rest before testing your strength against an apostle. A weapon cannot give you back the breath spent running.

Walk the outer ground first. Look for cover, lesser creatures and a way back before entering the keeper’s ground. Watch a heavy attack begin; move aside rather than trade blows through it. A retreat is not a broken oath. Return when your wounds and your equipment allow it, then examine what the fight uncovered.

A keeper holds a particular wound open. When it falls, examine that wound; a victory alone may leave the opening behind. Closing it restrains new crossings nearby. Creatures that have already crossed remain, and distant wounds still feed the dark. Take the evidence with you and read it before choosing another road.

The collision broke more than the ground. Some lives were drawn away from the deaths that awaited them. That does not make every being here a projection. Kill a living original and that life ends; breaking a reflection leaves its source untouched.

'Apostles are monstrous beings with wills and bodies of their own. The God Hand stand apart: they preside over the sacrifice. Void and Griffith are not ordinary apostles. Do not mistake surviving an encounter for defeating them.'
'Some things you met before were projections: an echo formed around a Behelit. Breaking the echo leaves the true being untouched. The Behelit itself was real.'

I follow a war older than your wounds. When I can deny the sacrifice another life, I do. That does not make your road mine to command. Keep the life I carried out of the dark; decide what is worth protecting with it.
